doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
title: Burned records and the Laines' houses
summary: Laine explains how he burned his dated records and talks about building his house in 1934 and the other places he owned.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All that stuff that I had put away, the roaches and mice and all got into it in the shed. I had to burn it. I had all that stuff almost dated. Up to the time, where, when, and how?
How long ago was it since you burned it, Dad?
burned it? How long ago since you burned it? Oh, I burned that
a long time ago. Oh, boy, a good while ago. A long time ago, yeah.

I built this place, you understand? 1934. I lived in it a while, you see. And I built another place in Florida Walk and... Florida Walk and... Not Montague. Cluitt. Florida Walk and Cluitt right over the bridge. The place behind there. Oh. Florida Walk and Cluitt. That's when she destroyed the whole lot of that place. Oh, yeah.

See? Yeah. I moved out of here because I had a French friend of mine who was to move out of here. and he would like to move in here. And after he moved, I kept this place empty for three or four solid years. I had that picture last week when you was here. I got rid of that place in Florida Walk. I actually give it away to keep a fella from being sent back to Germany. Yeah. Yeah. I think it was in this... I moved back in here then. See?
